title: FiDe: Reliable and Fast Crash Failure Detection to Boost Datacenter Coordination
problem: Machine crash detection in datacenters must balance detection speed (critical for maintaining consistency) against false positive rates that trigger incorrect failovers. Current failure detection mechanisms struggle to optimize both dimensions simultaneously.
motivation: Faster and more reliable crash detection improves datacenter system availability, reduces mean time to recovery, and enables better coordination of distributed recovery actions.
method: FiDe likely combines multiple detection signals (heartbeats, network probes, distributed consensus) with adaptive timeout mechanisms to distinguish genuine crashes from transient network delays. The system probably uses quorum-based verification across multiple monitoring nodes to reduce false positives while maintaining low detection latency.
key_novelty: Decoupled or adaptive detection strategy that addresses the speed-versus-reliability tradeoff separately rather than as a unified optimization problem.
contributions: A failure detection protocol balancing detection latency and reliability for datacenter environments
Mechanisms to reduce false positive detection rates through coordinated multi-source verification
Demonstration of improved datacenter coordination and recovery times
limitations: Specific mechanisms, evaluation results, and system scope not discussed in title alone.
primary_theme: Fast and reliable crash detection for datacenters
